Understanding Reading Skills


Reading skills                                                             Website
                                                                           www.beanurse.co.uk
Skimming
                                                                           Facebook
Skimming is reading quickly, running one’s eyes over the text to get the   https://www.facebook.com
                                                                           /vplanguages
most important information, or ‘gist’. You run your eyes over the text,
noting important information. Use skimming to find out quickly about       FREE Facebook Group
the topic of a text. You don’t have to understand each word when           https://www.facebook.co
                                                                           m/groups/beanurseuk
skimming.
Examples:
   Looking at the newspaper to get a general idea of the news
   Looking at a magazine to decide which articles you would like to
   read in more detail
   Looking at a travel brochures to get a quick impression of a holiday


Scanning


Scanning is reading quickly and searching for a specific piece of
information. You run your eyes over the text looking for the particular
piece of information you need. Use scanning when looking at
timetables, agendas, TV guides and so on, in order to find the details
you need. If you see words or phrases that you don't understand,
                                                                           Regards,
ignore them.
Examples:
   A TV guide.
   A train timetable                                                       Valentina Popescu
                                                                           EFL Teacher - OET Prep Provider
   A hotel guide
                                                                           Teacher Educator
                                                                           Coach within Education
 
Understanding Reading Skills


Reading skills                                                                Website
                                                                              www.beanurse.co.uk
Extensive reading
Extensive reading is often ‘reading for pleasure’ rather than reading a       Facebook
text set by the teacher. In this kind of reading an overall understanding     https://www.facebook.com
                                                                              /vplanguages
of a longer piece of text is sought - perhaps a story or an article. A good
reader worries less about individual words and sentences and gets             FREE Facebook Group
caught up in the general flow of a piece. S/he wants to get the main          https://www.facebook.co
                                                                              m/groups/beanurseuk
ideas and also often react personally to what has been read.
Examples:
    A biography of a sports hero of yours
    A novel you read before going to bed
    Magazine articles that interest you


Intensive reading
Intensive reading is accurate reading for detail. It is typically used with
short sections or sentences when the reader needs to understand or
study information or language use. Close attention is paid to a text and
its implications, and to the relationship of ideas within the text. A good
reader will also relate the text to their own schemata. In the case of
intensive reading it is important to understand each word, number or
fact.
                                                                              Regards,
Examples:
    A paragraph on philosophy
    A dense letter from the bank
    A contract                                                                Valentina Popescu
                                                                              EFL Teacher - OET Prep Provider
    A poem
                                                                              Teacher Educator
                                                                              Coach within Education
